clue.text: Presence of cleaner is followed by mother

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is an old British word for a cleaning lady
taken as written
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: The cleaner shows up, and then mum arrives too.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning woman, a common crossword stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence in the sense of a magnetic personal quality that commands attention is a synonym for charisma.

blocks.note: short for circa, Latin for about
standard abbreviation for right
standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Asking whether this is roughly the right day for the setter, who signs himself Joker.
explanation.walkthrough: Joker is also this puzzle's setter, which makes the question mark playful; a joker is one of the cards in a pack, and a card is also a joker, a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is a playing card, and a card is an amusing, eccentric person, so either sense fits.

indicators.note: something leaving a word is taken out of it, so those letters go

blocks.note: a man's name standing for any chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks away from a pile of aggregate, the gravel used in building.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GREG out of AGGREGATE and AG + ATE remains: AGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious mineral, so it is a kind of stone.

blocks.note: to inter is to bury a body
a branch of an organisation is a section of it

explanation.surface: Bury looks like the Lancashire town with a branch line meeting the main railway.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury reads as the English town in Greater Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An intersection is a place where roads meet, which is a junction.

clue.text: Lose track of minute Hebridean island

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for minute
Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for whisky

explanation.surface: Losing your way on a tiny Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute reads as tiny, but it is the time unit, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it somewhere and forget where, losing track of it.

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for account
the usual short form of identification

explanation.surface: Slicing up an account's identification details.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting looks like a verb; it is the adjective for a sharp, wounding remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid remark is a cutting one: sharp, biting and hurtful in tone.

clue.text: Crown — gold one is used in court

indicators.note: something used in another thing is placed inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for court
or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golden crown worn at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as or comes from heraldry, the language of coats of arms, where tinctures have French names.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles, so it is a kind of crown.

blocks.note: something dead is no longer in use
a railway line

explanation.surface: Asking when a railway will finally be closed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition; a dead line is also a closed railway, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the latest time by which a task must be finished.

clue.text: Bit inside leg, unfortunately not easy to eat?

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is things going wrong, so these letters end up in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bit of food lodged inside a leg of meat makes it hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestible food is hard to digest, so unpleasant or difficult to eat; the question mark admits the loose fit.

indicators.note: the insides of words are their middles, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: the inner letters of from
the inner letters of pasty, ignoring the apostrophe s

explanation.surface: The meat filling taken out of a pasty, a Cornish pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: From looks like a link word, but its insides count too. A pasty is a pastry case filled with meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.

clue.text: Performed song about drink in Spain

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for song is read backwards

blocks.note: performed a song, as a singer does
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone sang a song about drinking while on holiday in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is the Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and soda, a drink associated with Spain.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: material in the sense of physical, actual
a production is a creation

explanation.surface: Fabric needed for staging a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Material looks like cloth, and production like a stage show; both are misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreational means relating to leisure and amusement, which is what 'of play' describes.

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged
about here means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A resident gives an odd explanation about where they park.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is a person living in or occupying a place, a synonym of resident.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, so the short word sits within the verb

blocks.note: to nibble is a light way to chew
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nut, the kind of thing you nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a kidney-shaped tropical nut, eaten roasted as a snack.

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so these letters come out in a messy order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An athlete ran past, struggling terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan conditions are austere and harsh, after the tough ancient Greek city of Sparta, so hard fits.

clue.text: Defeated British eight are then eliminated nearly at the beginning

indicators.note: at the beginning points to the start of each word, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for British
the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A British rowing eight lose and are knocked out, almost from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliminated and nearly look like instructions to delete, but they only supply their first letters. An eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten is to be defeated in a contest; both are past participles.

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Sleeping on the family's bed linen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, on means placed above, so the sleep comes first. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a small square of linen for the table; calling it a sheet stretches the word, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I've cut tartan badly — not a pretty sight

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so these letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone admits they have hacked the tartan cloth and it looks awful. Tartan is the checked Scottish woollen pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unattractive is ugly or displeasing to look at, which is not a pretty sight.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the letter

blocks.note: vice is wicked or immoral behaviour
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A speech about immorality, perhaps by Oscar Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: Voice is the faculty of speech, or the expression of opinion, so it matches speech.

clue.text: Sensed the texture of thick material

blocks.note: first meaning: touched, past tense of the verb
second meaning: a dense pressed woollen fabric

explanation.surface: Running a hand over heavy cloth to judge it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of feel and the name of a matted wool fabric.

clue.text: Illustrations of rook pair in Noah's ship

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the earlier pieces sit within the vessel

blocks.note: R is the chess notation for a rook
a pair is two
Noah built the ark

explanation.surface: Pictures of a pair of rooks boarding Noah's Ark, two by two.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook looks like the bird, fitting the animals entering two by two, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork means the pictures and illustrations in a publication.

clue.text: French cheese injected with British sweetener

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the cheese holds the abbreviation

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: French cheese doctored with a British sweetening agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetener looks like sugar substitute; it is slang for a payment that wins someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement, often money, offered to win favour, which is a bribe.

indicators.note: putting back means turning to face the other way, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: a and an are the same article
a nut is a fanatic, as in health nut

explanation.surface: An angler who loves fishing throws a fish back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Fashionable church in hollow is dirty

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the church abbreviation sits within the hollow

blocks.note: in means in fashion
a dent is a hollow in a surface
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A trendy church in a valley turns out to be grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty in the sense of smutty or obscene matches indecent.
